steps.what: 10. RelicCmd.Remove/Replace/Melt: Remove awaits `relic.AfterRemoved()`; Replace removes the original and re-Obtains the replacement AT THE ORIGINAL'S LIST INDEX (preserving relic-list position); Melt marks the relic melted and also awaits AfterRemoved (RelicCmd.cs:61-93).
steps.rationale: The sim has no shared RelicCmd-equivalent command -- every removal site is a bare `run.relics.remove(...)` (events/ranwid_the_elder.py, events/relic_trader.py, relics/toy_box.py, conformance/runner.py). This is faithful-by-vacuity for AfterRemoved: `grep -rn "override.*Task AfterRemoved" src/Core/Models/Relics` returns ZERO matches -- no relic in the entire decompiled game overrides it, so its base no-op body means the sim's omission diverges from nothing observable. For Replace specifically: its two real C# callers (SwordOfStone.cs:48, TouchOfOrobas.cs:160) ARE ported, and BOTH preserve the index exactly as RelicCmd.Replace does -- `run.relics[run.relics.index(old)] = new` followed by `new.after_obtained(run)` (relics/sword_of_stone.py, relics/touch_of_orobas.py) -- verified by reading both files against their C# counterparts. For the plain-Remove sites: checked the C# behind both ported consumers (RanwidTheElder.cs:128, RelicTrader.cs:148-149) and confirmed BOTH use Remove+Obtain-with-default-index (i.e. append), matching the sim's remove+append exactly -- Ranwid/Relic Trader were NOT Replace calls in the source either, so no index-preservation was ever expected there. No currently-ported content is observably affected by the absence of a shared command.
